subject: Human Evolution
title: Hammerstones and Anvils
description: A 60-second lesson on Hammerstones and Anvils.

hook.text: Making a sharp flake isn't random bashing. You need a hammerstone, an anvil, and the right angle.

buildup.text: Strike too flat and nothing happens. Too steep and the core shatters into useless fragments.

discovery.text: The ideal striking angle is about 45 degrees. Early knappers learned this through trial and error.

twist.text: Some sites show piles of failed attempts. Learning was messy, and practice areas were shared.

climax.text: The physics of fracture mechanics governed tool-making long before any human understood physics.

punchline.text: They mastered physics without knowing it existed.

quiz.question: What is needed to make an effective stone flake?
options: Correct striking angle and controlled force
